text:
Amanda: Quick Q — we're staring down Q3 reserved GPU commits. Need a region-by-region thumb for 8x A100-equivalent capacity (steady inference workload). Focus: committed price, egress exposure, preempt/spot risk, and procurement lead time. TL;DRs please.
Karthik: OK — did a quick skim of cloud quotes + our usage curves. Short version: us-east has the cheapest committed unit price and lowest egress to our US customers; eu-west is ~10% more, but we have a negotiated enterprise add-on there; ap-southeast is most expensive + higher egress.
Maria: Also call out latency to EU customers (we need <60ms p95 for chat). eu-west helps avoid cross-region tail latency.
Eli: For embedding-heavy traffic we could mix A10G-like SKUs in ap-southeast for cost, but that hurts long-context gen. Worth considering for regional embedding caches.
billing-bot: FYI: current enterprise discount in eu-west1 = 7% on committed usage (applies to sustained commit only). No guaranteed discounts in ap-southeast in current contract.
Karthik: I put a tiny calc together (simplified):
```
# dollars per GPU-hour (illustrative)
us-east: on-demand 24.0 -> committed 17.0 (≈29% savings)
eu-west: on-demand 27.0 -> committed 18.9 (≈30% savings)
ap-southeast: on-demand 31.0 -> committed 22.0 (≈29% savings)
# egress penalty (per TB/month)
us-east -> users: low; eu-west -> moderate; ap-southeast -> high (+20% cost)
# naive break-even (months) for 12mo commit vs on-demand at our forecast
us-east: ~8-9 months
eu-west (with 7% extra): ~6-7 months
ap-southeast: ~12-14 months
```
Amanda: Nice. Two follow-ups: (1) how brittle is capacity in each region (can we get the committed vms/kernels we want on timeline)? (2) if we do multi-region fails over, what's the egress hit for cross-region KV/cache rehydration?
infra-bot: Capacity note: us-east fleet availability = high for A100-like SKUs. eu-west availability = medium; procurement lead ~3-6 weeks for reserved pools. ap-southeast availability = low for large contiguous commitments; expect 8+ weeks or need to accept alternate GPU models.
Julian: Cross-region cache rehydration: if we fail EU->US we estimate ~0.5-1.2TB/day per 100k active sessions depending on prefix/cache hit. That scales egress fast and adds latency.
Maria: That matters for SLOs. If we place majority in us-east and route EU traffic cross-region during outages, p95 likely doubles. Not acceptable.
Eli: Ops suggestion — commit baseline in-region per major market to protect SLO, then keep a small cross-region hot-standby for short-term spikes. Use async KV warmup to reduce rehydration volume.
Karthik: Quick proposal from the numbers + constraints: commit 40% capacity in us-east (cheap + availability), 40% in eu-west (SLO + discounted commit), 20% in ap-southeast (smaller commit, accept mixed SKUs). Keep a 10% global burst pool on low-cost spot-ish capacity for short-lived surges.
Amanda: Can you run the NPV-ish test quickly: with expected utilization 70% steady plus 20% seasonal spikes, does that allocation give cost + SLO wins vs 100% us-east commit + cross-region failover?
Karthik: Rough NPV: 3-year window, discount 6% annual, factoring egress & discount. Short answer: multi-region commit wins on SLO and gives modest cost delta (~+3% spend) vs single-region commit once you add expected cross-region egress and SLA penalties. If SLO breaches cost >5% of revenue (conservative), multi-region is strictly better.
billing-bot: Note: any multi-region commit will need territory-specific contracts; eu-west requires an amendment to apply current negotiated term to the new capacity. Lead legal ~2 weeks.
Maria: Ops risk: ap-southeast mixed SKUs means one code path for quantized models, another for large-precision gen. That's technical debt if we scale.
Eli: We can mitigate by putting embedding-only traffic on cheaper SKUs and keep gen-models centralized in us/eu. That reduces ap egress and lowers commit size.
Amanda: Sounds like we're converging. Actionables: (1) Karthik to prepare a 12-month committed ordering plan by region + NPV spreadsheet (2) infra to confirm procurement timeline for the exact SKUs (3) legal to draft eu-west amendment (4) product/ops to validate SLO routing plan.
Julian: I'll scope the cache warmup plan and estimate egress for worst-case failover. ETA 48h.
Karthik: I'll post the spreadsheet in the thread later today — will include sensitivity to spot availability and 6/12/36 month commit lengths.
Amanda: Thanks — vote: :thumbsup: if you agree with the 40/40/20 split + small global burst. Anyone object?
Maria: :thumbsup:
Eli: :thumbsup:
Julian: :thumbsup: (pending cache numbers)
